procedural_history.originating_court: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate (inferred from paragraph 12)
procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and Order dated 29.10.2010 of the High Court of Judicature at Allahabad in SA No. 896 of 2005
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The High Court of Judicature at Allahabad issued a Judgment and Order on 29.10.2010 in SA No. 896 of 2005.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The Appellant, being aggrieved by the High Court's Judgment and Order dated 29.10.2010, appealed to the Supreme Court in Civil Appeal No. 5902 of 2012. The Supreme Court allowed the appeal.

directions: The order of the learned Single Judge and the impugned order of the Division Bench dated 29.10.2010 in Special Appeal No. 896/2005 are set aside.
The order of 12.04.2005 of the third respondent, Commandant 27th Battalion, PAC, Sitapur is quashed and set aside.

The respondents are directed to appoint the appellant in service on the post of Constable for which he was selected, pursuant to his participation in reference to the Recruitment Notification dated 20.01.2004.
The appellant will not be entitled for the arrears of salary for the period during which he has not served the force.
The appellant will be entitled for all notional benefits, including pay, seniority and other consequential benefits.
Necessary orders shall be passed within a period of four weeks from today.
There shall be no order as to costs.

issue.issue_text: Was the State justified in cancelling the selection of the appellant, vide its order of 12.04.2005?

facts: The appellant was selected for the post of constable.
After applying but before selection, he was involved in a criminal case in which he was ultimately acquitted.
In a subsequent verification affidavit, the appellant did not disclose the fact of this criminal case.
The State cancelled his selection via an order dated 12.04.2005, citing the non-disclosure and filing of a false affidavit.

Despite this, the official character verification reports from the SHO and the Superintendent of Police noted the acquittal, certified the appellant's character as "excellent," and found him eligible for government service.
law: The Court relied on its precedents, particularly *Satish Chandra Yadav*, which established that not every non-disclosure of a criminal case automatically disqualifies a candidate.
An appointing authority cannot act mechanically; it must consider the overall suitability of the candidate for the post.
A broad-brush approach of disqualifying every candidate for non-disclosure is unjust. Each case must be decided on its own facts and circumstances, taking a holistic view.
Recruitment rules allowing for cancellation due to concealment must be read in the context of this established case law.
application: The Court found that the Appointing Authority had acted "mechanically" by cancelling the selection solely because the affidavit contained incorrect facts.

The authority failed to consider the appellant's suitability for the job, ignoring the positive character verification reports from senior police officials which recommended him for service despite being aware of the acquitted case.

Applying the principles from its precedents, the Court determined that the cancellation order was "neither fair nor reasonable" as it was oblivious to the ground realities of the case, such as the acquittal and the excellent character report.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court concluded that the State was not justified in cancelling the appellant's selection. It found the cancellation order of 12.04.2005 to be unfair, unreasonable, and mechanical. Therefore, the Court quashed the order and directed the State to appoint the appellant to the post of Constable.

issue.issue_text: To what relief, if any, is the appellant entitled to?

reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court granted partial relief to the appellant. The Court allowed the appeal, setting aside the lower court's judgment and quashing the order that had cancelled the appellant's selection or discharged them from service. It directed the respondents to reinstate or appoint the appellant to the post of Constable. However, the Court specified that the appellant was not entitled to any back wages or arrears of salary for the period they were out of service. While denying back pay, the Court did grant the appellant all "notional benefits," including seniority, pay, and other consequential benefits, as if they had been in service continuously.

arguments.issue_text: Was the State justified in cancelling the selection of the appellant, vide its order of 12.04.2005?
appellant_arguments: There was no willful concealment of information.
At the time of submitting the application form on 12.02.2004, no criminal case was pending against the appellant, and there was no requirement to furnish an affidavit at that stage.
The appellant was acquitted in the criminal case on 13.09.2004, which was before the affidavit was filed on 30.10.2004.
Since no criminal case was pending when the affidavit was filed, the appellant was under a bona fide belief that there was no need to disclose the past case.
There was no intention to deceive.
respondent_arguments: The appellant made a false representation in Clauses 4, 5, 6, and 7 of his affidavit.
The State acted consistently, as two other persons who also gave false statements had their selections cancelled.
The cancellation is justified by the precedent set in the case of Avtar Singh Vs. Union of India and Others.

arguments.issue_text: To what relief, if any, is the appellant entitled to?
appellant_arguments: The appellant is entitled to relief as the cancellation of his selection was not justified due to the lack of willful concealment and his acquittal prior to the submission of the affidavit.
respondent_arguments: The appellant is not entitled to any relief because he made a false representation in his affidavit, and the cancellation was justified.

cases.case_name: Ram Kumar vs. State of U.P. and Others
cases.principle: That the power to cancel a candidature is not to be dealt with arbitrarily and the exercise of power has to be in a reasonable manner with objectivity, having due regard to the facts of the case.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: An employer's exercise of power must not be arbitrary and must be exercised in a reasonable and objective manner, having due regard to the facts of the case. The employer is required to take into consideration the government orders, instructions, and rules applicable to the employee at the time of making the decision.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: While a candidate is required to furnish correct information, the employer's power to cancel a selection for non-disclosure is not absolute and cannot be exercised mechanically. The authority must act judiciously, reasonably, and with objectivity, having due regard to the specific facts of the case. A mere suppression of information, especially regarding a minor criminal case that resulted in acquittal before the verification stage, does not automatically justify cancellation of candidature. The authority must consider the nature of the post, the nature of the duties, and the overall suitability of the candidate, rather than applying a rigid rule.
legal_tests_applied: The candidate who has suppressed material information or made a false declaration has a right not to be dealt with arbitrarily, and the power to cancel candidature must be judiciously exercised by the competent authority in a reasonable manner with objectivity, having due regard to the facts of the case on hand.
The yardstick for adjudging suitability depends on the nature of the post, nature of duties, and the effect of the suppression on that suitability; no hard and fast rule of thumb can be laid down.
The seriousness of the original offense must be considered, with a more lenient view to be taken for offenses that are not of a serious nature like murder, dacoity, or rape.
why_appellant_lost: The appellant was denied arrears of salary for the period he did not serve, based on the principle that he is not entitled to pay for a period during which he has not worked for the force.
why_respondent_won: The respondent succeeded in avoiding the payment of back wages, as the court directed that the appellant would not be entitled to arrears of salary for the period he was out of service.
policy_considerations: Employment opportunities are a scarce commodity in our country.
There cannot be any mechanical or rhetorical incantation of moral turpitude to deny appointment simplicitor; much will depend on the facts of a case.

Every individual deserves an opportunity to improve, learn from the past and move ahead in life by self-improvement. To make past conduct, irrespective of all considerations, an albatross around the neck of the candidate, may not always constitute justice.
